post.description: Local/demo-only platform persona login; hidden with 404 elsewhere.

Authenticate user and return JWT tokens (also set as httpOnly cookies).

When 2FA is enabled on the account the response contains
``require_2fa=True`` and a short-lived ``mfa_token`` instead of
access/refresh tokens.

P0 -1 — locked down against brute force: a sliding window of 5 attempts
per 15 minutes per client IP (the budget the rate_limiter module documents
for the login endpoint). Unlike the ``@rate_limit`` decorator (which needs
a starlette Response return) this endpoint keeps the ``response_model``
serialization and calls :func:`enforce_rate_limit` directly.

get.description: Return the current user's info + permissions.

post.description:
Sign the user out of **every** device (including this one).

Requires authentication. Revokes all of the user's sessions and blacklists
the presented access/refresh tokens. The next request from any device fails
authentication once its short-lived access token expires (or immediately for
tokens blacklisted here).

Revoke the presented access token (and refresh token, if supplied).

Tokens are blacklisted by ``jti`` until their natural expiry, so they can
no longer be used even though the JWT itself remains cryptographically
valid. Auth cookies are cleared in all cases.

Change the current user's password.

Validates the new password against the password policy (strength,
blocklist, HIBP breach check). Revokes all existing sessions for this user
so the new password takes effect everywhere immediately.

Returns a ``Response`` because the ``rate_limit`` decorator attaches
rate-limit headers to the returned object.

Email a single-use password-reset link (public endpoint).

The response is identical whether or not the account exists, so this
endpoint cannot be used to enumerate users. Rate-limited to slow abuse.

Consume a password-reset token and set a new password (public endpoint).

On success every device session is revoked and outstanding JWTs are
blacklisted, so old sessions are signed out immediately.

Consume a tenant-admin invitation token and set the first password (public).

The invitation token comes from the super-admin invite email (P3 -4.2).
Only passwordless accounts can be activated this way; already-activated
accounts must use the forgot-password flow.

Begin enrolling an authenticator app.

Generates a fresh shared secret and stores it in the *pending* state —
2FA is not active until the user confirms with a code from their authenticator
app via :endpoint:`confirm_two_factor`.

Confirm a pending 2FA setup with the current TOTP code.

Activates 2FA, replaces the pending secret with the active one, and returns
one-time recovery codes that are only ever shown once.
Disable 2FA — requires a valid TOTP or recovery code first.

Replace all recovery codes — old ones are revoked immediately.

Requires a valid TOTP or an existing recovery code for authorization.

Complete a login that required 2FA.

Validates the ``mfa_token`` from the login step and the ``token`` provided
by the user (TOTP or recovery code). On success issues the normal JWT
access/refresh token pair and sets them as httpOnly cookies.

P0 -1 — TOTP guessing is throttled (10 attempts / 15 min per client IP).

get.description:

post.description:
